architecture.mechanism: During a cold-start range change from neutral or reverse to a forward range, the transmission control apparatus first shifts the gear stage down to a low-speed stage before progressing through the normal gear-engagement sequence, smoothing the initial engagement torque and reducing shift variability.
architecture.intervention: Have the dealer reflash or update the Transmission Control Module (TCM) calibration so that the cold-start forward-range engagement sequence executes a temporary downshift to a low-speed stage prior to ramping up through the forward gear ratios, rather than engaging the target forward gear directly from rest.
architecture.expected_effect: Eliminates the erratic/abrupt shift feel on cold startups by damping engagement torque and equalizing clutch-fill pressure during the first forward-range engagement after a cold soak; behavior after warm-up remains unchanged.
architecture.falsification_test: Cold-soak the vehicle (ambient < 0 °C / 32 °F) for at least 8 hours, then, with the TCM in the updated calibration, perform 10 consecutive D-range engagements from N or R at idle (brake held, engine running) and measure the time-to-engagement, engagement shock (accelerometer on transmission tunnel), and any reported flare/slip events; compare to the pre-reflash baseline recorded on the same vehicle under identical conditions — success is defined as engagement-shock standard deviation reduced by ≥ 50% and absence of reported flare across all 10 trials.
